items.subject: eng

skill.th: การตอบรับคำขอบคุณ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: Thanks so much for helping me move house last weekend.
B: ______ That's what friends are for.

explanation.en: "Don't mention it" is a standard reply to thanks. "It doesn't matter" answers an apology or a problem, "Same here" agrees with a feeling, and "I'm afraid not" is a polite no.
explanation.th: Don't mention it เป็นคำตอบมาตรฐานเมื่อมีคนขอบคุณ ส่วน It doesn't matter ใช้ตอบคำขอโทษหรือบอกว่าไม่สำคัญ Same here ใช้บอกว่ารู้สึกเหมือนกัน และ I'm afraid not เป็นการปฏิเสธอย่างสุภาพ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การปฏิเสธคำชวนอย่างสุภาพ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: Do you fancy going to the night market after school?
B: ______ I've got a mountain of homework tonight.
choices: I'd love to, but I can't.
That would be lovely, see you there.

explanation.en: Homework is B's reason for not going, so B must decline: "I'd love to, but I can't". The other three accept the invitation, which contradicts the reason given.
explanation.th: การบ้านเป็นเหตุผลที่ B ไปไม่ได้ จึงต้องปฏิเสธ I'd love to, but I can't อีกสามตัวเลือกเป็นการตอบรับ ซึ่งขัดกับเหตุผลที่ให้ไว้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การเข้าใจสำนวนเกี่ยวกับอนาคต

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: I heard you got the scholarship to study in Canada. Congratulations!
B: Thanks, but ______ I'm still waiting for my visa.
choices: I'm not counting my chickens yet.
I'm over the moon about the visa.
it's all water under the bridge.

explanation.en: "Don't count your chickens (before they hatch)" means don't be sure of success too early, which fits B still waiting for a visa. B is not happy about the visa yet, "water under the bridge" means a past problem that no longer matters, and "burn your bridges" means destroy your chance to go back.
explanation.th: สำนวน don't count your chickens หมายถึงอย่าเพิ่งมั่นใจว่าจะสำเร็จ ตรงกับที่ B ยังรอวีซ่าอยู่ B ยังไม่ได้ดีใจเรื่องวีซ่า water under the bridge คือเรื่องที่ผ่านไปแล้ว และ burn your bridges คือการทำลายโอกาสที่จะย้อนกลับ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การแสดงความไม่เห็นด้วยแบบทางการ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: Honestly, I don't see why we need to learn history. It's all in the past.
B: ______ Understanding the past helps us avoid repeating the same mistakes.
choices: I couldn't have put it better myself.
You took the words right out of my mouth.
Fair enough, you've got a point.
I'm afraid I'd have to disagree.

explanation.en: B goes on to defend history, so B disagrees: "I'm afraid I'd have to disagree". The other three all agree with A, which contradicts B's next sentence.
explanation.th: B กล่าวต่อเพื่อปกป้องวิชาประวัติศาสตร์ จึงไม่เห็นด้วย I'm afraid I'd have to disagree อีกสามตัวเลือกล้วนเห็นด้วยกับ A ซึ่งขัดกับประโยคถัดไปของ B

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การตอบรับข้อเสนอ

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: Would you like me to drop you off at the station?
B: ______ I could do with a lift; it's pouring.
choices: Don't bother, I'd rather get wet.
That would be great, if it's no trouble.

explanation.en: B wants a lift ("I could do with a lift"), so B accepts politely: "That would be great, if it's no trouble". "No, I wouldn't like" is ungrammatical and refuses, "Don't bother" refuses, and "Yes, drop me" is incomplete and sounds rude.
explanation.th: B ต้องการให้ไปส่ง (I could do with a lift) จึงตอบรับอย่างสุภาพ That would be great, if it's no trouble ส่วน No, I wouldn't like ผิดไวยากรณ์และเป็นการปฏิเสธ Don't bother ก็ปฏิเสธ และ Yes, drop me ไม่สมบูรณ์และฟังห้วน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การเตือนโดยใช้สำนวน

topic.th: บทสนทนาในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the best response to complete the conversation.
A: This term I've agreed to organise the charity concert, coach the junior debate team and edit the school magazine.
B: ______ You'll wear yourself out.
choices: Aren't you biting off more than you can chew?
Aren't you just sitting on the fence?
Haven't you let the cat out of the bag?
Isn't that a piece of cake for you?

explanation.en: "Bite off more than you can chew" means take on more than you can manage, which matches three big jobs and the warning "You'll wear yourself out". "Sit on the fence" means avoid choosing, "let the cat out of the bag" means reveal a secret, and "a piece of cake" (easy) contradicts the warning.
explanation.th: bite off more than you can chew แปลว่ารับงานเกินกำลัง ตรงกับการรับงานใหญ่สามอย่างและคำเตือนว่าจะเหนื่อยจนหมดแรง ส่วน sit on the fence แปลว่าไม่ยอมเลือกข้าง let the cat out of the bag แปลว่าเผยความลับ และ a piece of cake (ง่ายมาก) ขัดกับคำเตือน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: กริยาวลี lay off

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The factory had to ______ two hundred workers when sales collapsed."

explanation.en: "Lay off" means dismiss workers because there is not enough work, which matches collapsing sales. "Lay out" means arrange or spend, "lay down" means put down or establish rules, and "lay by" means save.
explanation.th: lay off แปลว่าเลิกจ้างเพราะงานไม่พอ ตรงกับยอดขายตก ส่วน lay out แปลว่าจัดวางหรือใช้จ่าย lay down แปลว่าวางลงหรือกำหนดกฎ และ lay by แปลว่าเก็บออม

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คุณศัพท์ระดับสูงที่ใช้บรรยายคำอธิบาย

topic.th: ความหมายคำและการสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Her explanation was so ______ that nobody in the class could follow it."

explanation.en: Nobody could follow it, so the explanation was too complicated: "convoluted". "Concise" (short and clear), "coherent" (logical) and "lucid" (clear) all describe explanations that are easy to follow.
explanation.th: ไม่มีใครตามทัน แสดงว่าคำอธิบายซับซ้อนวกวน คือ convoluted ส่วน concise (กระชับ) coherent (เป็นเหตุเป็นผล) และ lucid (ชัดเจน) ล้วนหมายถึงคำอธิบายที่เข้าใจง่าย

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำปรากฏร่วม grave danger

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Scientists have warned that the coral reef is in ______ danger of disappearing within twenty years."

explanation.en: "In grave danger" is the fixed collocation for very serious danger. "Heavy", "strong" and "deep" do not combine with danger (we say heavy rain, strong wind, deep trouble).
explanation.th: in grave danger เป็นคำปรากฏร่วมตายตัว หมายถึงอันตรายร้ายแรง ส่วน heavy, strong, deep ไม่ใช้กับ danger (ใช้ heavy rain, strong wind, deep trouble)

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Meaning of formal adjectives in context
skill.th: ความหมายของคุณศัพท์ทางการตามบริบท

topic.th: ความหมายคำและการสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the meaning closest to "ambiguous" in the sentence.
"The minister's statement was deliberately ambiguous, so journalists could not tell whether the policy would change."
choices: open to more than one interpretation

explanation.en: Journalists could not tell what the policy would be, so the statement could be understood in different ways: "ambiguous" means open to more than one interpretation. Detail, hostility or falseness would not cause this uncertainty.
explanation.th: นักข่าวบอกไม่ได้ว่านโยบายจะเปลี่ยนหรือไม่ แสดงว่าคำแถลงตีความได้หลายทาง ambiguous จึงแปลว่ากำกวม ความละเอียด ความเป็นปรปักษ์ หรือความเท็จไม่ได้ทำให้เกิดความไม่แน่ใจแบบนี้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: กริยาวลี put up with

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"We can't ______ with this noise any longer; let's complain to the manager."

explanation.en: "Put up with" means tolerate, which fits complaining about noise. "Get on with" means have a good relationship or continue, "keep up with" means stay at the same level, and "come up with" means think of an idea.
explanation.th: put up with แปลว่าทนกับ เข้ากับการจะไปร้องเรียนเรื่องเสียงดัง ส่วน get on with แปลว่าเข้ากันได้หรือทำต่อไป keep up with แปลว่าตามให้ทัน และ come up with แปลว่าคิดออก

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การสร้างคำด้วยอุปสรรค dis-

topic.th: ความหมายคำและการสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The scientist's claims were ______ by later research, which found no evidence to support them."

explanation.en: "Discredit" means show that something is not true or not trustworthy, which matches "found no evidence". "Uncredited" means not given credit (e.g. in a film), "miscredited" is not a standard word, and "incredible" is an adjective meaning amazing.
explanation.th: discredit แปลว่าทำให้หมดความน่าเชื่อถือ ตรงกับการไม่พบหลักฐานสนับสนุน ส่วน uncredited แปลว่าไม่ได้รับการระบุชื่อ miscredited ไม่ใช่คำมาตรฐาน และ incredible เป็นคุณศัพท์แปลว่าน่าทึ่ง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำปรากฏร่วมระหว่างกริยาวิเศษณ์กับกริยา

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วมและกริยาวลี

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The charity relies ______ on donations from the public; without them it would have to close."

explanation.en: "Rely heavily on" is the natural collocation for depending a lot on something. "Strongly" goes with believe or recommend, "deeply" with care or regret, and "highly" with recommend or skilled.
explanation.th: rely heavily on เป็นคำปรากฏร่วมที่เป็นธรรมชาติ หมายถึงพึ่งพาอย่างมาก ส่วน strongly ใช้กับ believe, recommend deeply ใช้กับ care, regret และ highly ใช้กับ recommend หรือ skilled

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Word forms: noun after an article
skill.th: รูปคำ: คำนามหลัง article

topic.th: ความหมายคำและการสร้างคำ

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Her decision to leave the team came as a complete ______ to everyone."

explanation.en: After "a complete" we need a noun, and "come as a surprise" is a fixed phrase. "Surprising" and "surprised" are adjectives, and "surprisingly" is an adverb.
explanation.th: หลัง a complete ต้องเป็นคำนาม และ come as a surprise เป็นวลีตายตัว ส่วน surprising, surprised เป็นคุณศัพท์ และ surprisingly เป็นกริยาวิเศษณ์

items.subject: eng

skill.th: เงื่อนไขแบบที่ 3 รูปสลับที่

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและ wish

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Had the government acted sooner, the flooding ______ so severe."

explanation.en: "Had the government acted" = "If the government had acted", an unreal past condition about a past flood, so the result is "would not have been". "Would not be" refers to the present, and the other forms are not conditional results.
explanation.th: Had the government acted มีความหมายเท่ากับ If the government had acted เป็นเงื่อนไขที่ไม่จริงในอดีตเกี่ยวกับน้ำท่วมที่เกิดไปแล้ว ผลจึงเป็น would not have been ส่วน would not be หมายถึงปัจจุบัน และรูปอื่นไม่ใช่รูปผลของเงื่อนไข

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การสลับที่หลัง Never before

topic.th: ความสอดคล้อง การเปรียบเทียบ และการสลับที่

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"Never before ______ so many students apply for the scholarship."

explanation.en: A negative adverb like "Never before" at the start requires inversion: auxiliary + subject + verb, "had the school seen". Normal order is wrong after it, and "did … saw" uses two past forms.
explanation.th: เมื่อขึ้นต้นด้วยคำปฏิเสธอย่าง Never before ต้องสลับเป็นกริยาช่วย + ประธาน + กริยา คือ had the school seen ส่วนการเรียงแบบปกติผิด และ did … saw ใช้รูปอดีตซ้อนสองครั้ง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: future perfect continuous

topic.th: กาลของกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"By next June, I ______ English for ten years."

explanation.en: "By next June" is a future point, and "for ten years" is the period up to it, so the future perfect continuous "will have been studying" is needed. The other forms do not look back from a future point.
explanation.th: By next June เป็นจุดเวลาในอนาคต และ for ten years คือระยะเวลาจนถึงจุดนั้น จึงใช้ future perfect continuous คือ will have been studying ส่วนรูปอื่นไม่ได้มองย้อนจากจุดเวลาในอนาคต

items.subject: eng

skill.th: would rather + ประธาน + past simple

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและ wish

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"I'd rather you ______ anyone about the surprise party."

explanation.en: When "would rather" is followed by a different subject, the verb is in the past simple with present or future meaning: "I'd rather you didn't tell". Present, future and to-infinitive forms are not used.
explanation.th: เมื่อ would rather ตามด้วยประธานอีกคน กริยาจะใช้ past simple แต่มีความหมายปัจจุบันหรืออนาคต คือ I'd rather you didn't tell ส่วนรูปปัจจุบัน อนาคต และ to-infinitive ใช้ไม่ได้

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Passive reporting verbs with perfect infinitive
skill.th: passive reporting verb กับ perfect infinitive

topic.th: ประโยค passive และ causative

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"The bridge is thought ______ in the 14th century."

explanation.en: The belief is present (is thought) but the building happened in the past, and the bridge was built by people, so we need the perfect passive infinitive "to have been built". "To have built" is active, and "to be built" refers to the present or future.
explanation.th: ความเชื่อเป็นปัจจุบัน (is thought) แต่การสร้างเกิดในอดีต และสะพานถูกสร้าง จึงใช้ perfect passive infinitive คือ to have been built ส่วน to have built เป็น active และ to be built หมายถึงปัจจุบันหรืออนาคต

items.subject: eng

skill.th: participle clause รูป V3 แสดงความรู้สึก

topic.th: อนุประโยคสัมพันธ์และ participle clause

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"______ by the news, she couldn't say a word."

explanation.en: She was shocked by the news (passive meaning, "by the news"), so the past participle "Shocked" is correct. "Shocking" and "Having shocked" would mean she shocked someone, and "To shock" expresses purpose.
explanation.th: เธอตกใจเพราะข่าว (ความหมาย passive มี by the news) จึงใช้ V3 คือ Shocked ส่วน Shocking และ Having shocked หมายถึงเธอทำให้คนอื่นตกใจ และ To shock แสดงจุดประสงค์

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result
skill.th: mixed conditional เงื่อนไขอดีต ผลปัจจุบัน

topic.th: ประโยคเงื่อนไขและ wish

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"If I hadn't stayed up so late last night, I ______ so tired now."

explanation.en: The condition is past (hadn't stayed up last night) but the result is now, so this mixed conditional uses "wouldn't be". "Wouldn't have been" refers to a past result, and the other forms break the pattern.
explanation.th: เงื่อนไขอยู่ในอดีต (hadn't stayed up last night) แต่ผลเป็นปัจจุบัน (now) จึงใช้ mixed conditional คือ wouldn't be ส่วน wouldn't have been หมายถึงผลในอดีต และรูปอื่นผิดโครงสร้าง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: causative have something + V3 (เหตุการณ์ที่เกิดกับเรา)

topic.th: ประโยค passive และ causative

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"She had her purse ______ while she was waiting for the train."

explanation.en: "Have something + past participle" can describe something bad that someone did to you: "had her purse stolen". The other forms would mean she made someone steal it or are ungrammatical.
explanation.th: have something + V3 ใช้บอกเหตุการณ์ไม่ดีที่คนอื่นทำกับเรา คือ had her purse stolen ส่วนรูปอื่นหมายถึงเธอให้คนอื่นขโมยหรือผิดไวยากรณ์

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การสลับที่ด้วย So + คุณศัพท์

topic.th: ความสอดคล้อง การเปรียบเทียบ และการสลับที่

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
"So ______ that the match had to be stopped."

explanation.en: When "So + adjective" starts the sentence, the verb comes before the subject: "So heavy was the rain that…". Normal order is used only in "The rain was so heavy that…".
explanation.th: เมื่อขึ้นต้นด้วย So + คุณศัพท์ ต้องวางกริยาไว้หน้าประธาน คือ So heavy was the rain that… การเรียงแบบปกติใช้ได้เฉพาะในรูป The rain was so heavy that…

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การรายงานคำสั่ง

topic.en: Verb patterns, modals and reported speech
topic.th: รูปแบบกริยา modal และคำพูดรายงาน

items.stem:
Choose the best option to complete the sentence.
""Don't touch the wires," the electrician said. → The electrician told us ______ the wires."

explanation.en: A negative command is reported with tell + object + not + to-infinitive: "told us not to touch". "Don't touch" keeps the direct form, and the -ing forms are wrong after tell + object.

items.passage:
The Disappearing Night

For most of human history, the night sky was one of the great shared experiences of our species. On a clear night, almost anyone could look up and see thousands of stars and the pale band of the Milky Way. Today, more than a third of the world's population can no longer see the Milky Way from where they live, and in some heavily developed regions the figure is far higher. The cause is light pollution: the excessive or badly directed artificial light that now spills from streetlights, buildings, billboards and car parks into the sky.

Astronomers were among the first to raise the alarm, since a bright sky makes faint objects impossible to observe. But the consequences extend well beyond science. Many animals depend on the natural cycle of light and darkness to find food, navigate and reproduce. Newly hatched sea turtles, for example, find the ocean by moving towards the brightest horizon, which on an undeveloped beach is the moonlit sea. On a beach backed by hotels, however, the hatchlings often crawl inland, where they die of exhaustion or are caught by predators. Migrating birds, which use the stars to navigate, are drawn towards lit-up towers, and large numbers are killed each year in collisions.

Humans are affected too. Exposure to bright light at night, particularly the blue-rich light produced by many LEDs, suppresses the production of melatonin, the hormone that regulates sleep. Some researchers have suggested links between long-term exposure and health problems, although these connections are not yet fully understood.

Unlike many environmental problems, light pollution is remarkably easy to reverse. A polluted river may take decades to recover, but a light that is switched off stops polluting instantly. Simple measures—shielding streetlights so that they point downwards, using warmer colours, and dimming or turning off lights that are not needed late at night—can dramatically reduce the problem while also cutting energy bills. Several towns around the world have gained "dark sky" status by adopting such rules, and some now attract tourists who come specifically to see the stars.

The real obstacle, then, is not technology but awareness. Few people think of light as a pollutant at all; for most of us, a brightly lit street simply feels safe and modern. Changing that perception may prove harder than changing the bulbs.
items.stem: What is the main point of the passage?
choices: LED lights should be banned in all cities.
Astronomers are the main victims of light pollution.
Light pollution harms nature and people but could be reduced fairly easily.
Dark-sky towns have become popular tourist destinations.

explanation.en: The passage describes effects on astronomy, animals and humans, then stresses that the problem is "remarkably easy to reverse". It never calls for an LED ban, says the consequences go beyond astronomers, and mentions dark-sky tourism only as a detail.

The Map

When my grandfather died, he left me three things: a wristwatch that ran ten minutes slow, a box of cassette tapes I had no way of playing, and a map. The map was drawn in blue ballpoint on the back of an old calendar, and it showed the neighbourhood in Thonburi where he had grown up. Every house, shop and tree was labelled in his tiny, careful handwriting: "Mr Lim's bicycle repairs", "big tamarind—climb here", "Auntie Pen's sweets (best coconut ice cream)".

For months, I left it in a drawer. Then one Sunday in the hot season, with nothing better to do, I took the boat across the river and tried to follow it.

I was not prepared for how little remained. Where Mr Lim's shop should have been, there was a convenience store with automatic doors that sighed open as I approached. The big tamarind had been replaced by a car park. I walked up and down the soi three times looking for Auntie Pen's, feeling increasingly foolish, before an old woman sitting in a doorway asked me whether I was lost.

I showed her the map. She held it very close to her face, then very far away, and then she began to laugh—a dry, delighted laugh that turned into a cough. "Somchai," she said, tapping my grandfather's name in the corner. "He used to steal mangoes from my father's tree."

Her name was Wan, and she was the daughter of the Auntie Pen on the map; the sweet shop had closed forty years ago. Yet she remembered my grandfather as a thin boy with enormous ears who could climb anything, and she spent the next two hours telling me stories about him that nobody in my family had ever heard.

By the time I left, the sun was setting over the river. I had not found a single place on the map. And yet, as the boat pulled away from the pier, I realised that I had found exactly what my grandfather would have wanted me to find, even if he could not have planned it himself. The map had never really been about places at all.
items.stem: Why did the narrator feel "increasingly foolish"?
choices: She had taken the wrong boat across the river.
The old woman was laughing at her.
She could not find any of the places on the map.
She had forgotten her grandfather's name.

explanation.en: Mr Lim's shop and the tamarind were gone, and she walked up and down the soi three times without finding Auntie Pen's. The boat is not described as wrong, the laughing came later and was about her grandfather, and the name is on the map.

items.passage:
More Roads, More Traffic

Whenever traffic in Bangkok becomes unbearable—which is to say, most weekdays—someone proposes the same solution: build more roads. Widen the highways, add another expressway, construct a new flyover. It seems like common sense. If there are too many cars for the space available, surely the answer is more space. Yet decades of evidence from cities around the world suggest that this answer is not merely ineffective but often counterproductive.

The reason is a phenomenon that transport researchers call "induced demand". When a new road opens, journeys along that route become faster, at least at first. But faster journeys encourage people to change their behaviour. Some who used to take the train start driving; others who avoided the trip altogether begin to make it; still others move further out of the city, knowing they can now commute by car. Within a few years, the new road is as congested as the old one was, except that there are now more cars in total. Studies in several countries have found that the distance driven in a city tends to rise roughly in proportion to the amount of new road built.

None of this means that cities should never build roads. A new road may be essential to connect a growing area that has no access at all. But as a strategy for reducing congestion, road-building has been tested repeatedly, and it has failed almost every time.

What works better? The cities that have made real progress against traffic have generally done so by making alternatives more attractive rather than by making driving easier. That means frequent, reliable public transport; safe, shaded routes for walking and cycling; and, more controversially, charging drivers to enter the busiest areas at peak times. London, Stockholm and Singapore have all introduced such charges, and in each case traffic fell noticeably soon afterwards.

Bangkok has already invested heavily in its rail network, and the results are visible in the crowds on its trains. The next step is harder, because it asks drivers to give something up. Politicians understandably prefer cutting ribbons on new flyovers to telling voters that driving should cost more. But if the city is serious about its traffic, it will have to stop treating the car as the solution to the problem rather than its cause.

choices: Traffic disappears permanently from the area.
People stop driving and take the train instead.
It attracts more drivers until it becomes congested again.
The old roads in the area are closed.

explanation.en: This is "induced demand": faster journeys attract new drivers, and "within a few years, the new road is as congested as the old one was". Traffic does not disappear, people move from trains to cars (not the reverse), and old roads are not mentioned as closing.
